text: Wolfenstein 3D is pure old school shooter fun. While the game features a few tricky levels, for the most part it is smartly designed to deliver maximum Nazi killing fun. It might be old, but this game's still got some bite to it. As one of the shooters that helped put id Software on the map, it is a piece of gaming history. title: Wolfenstein 3D
text: BEST ABOUT IT:  Exterminating Nazis in THREE DEE! WORST ABOUT IT:  The nauseating early 3-D graphics.  Getting flanked by a Nazi and not being able to turn fast enough or one that shoots you from behind a door before the door even opens enough to see them.  Or those planters that they deviously colored just like the Nazis. GAMEPLAY:  The great grand-daddy of FPS.  You navigate a series of mazes to find an elevator and any keys needed to open the doors that block it and are scored at the end of each based on your time, kills, and secrets found.  You're armed with a knife and the 3 guns you can pick up. (pistol, submachine gun, and Gatling-gun).  You can only carry 99 bullets so ammo is always a concern, especially since all your guns share the same rounds and the automatics burn them fast, but that's part of the game's core design.  Many secret passages contain guns and ammo but there's no hint to what walls open, so you just have to rub against them all. CONTROLS:  You can turn left and right and also strafe by holding shift but you cannot look or aim vertically.  It doesn’t seem too picky about your horizontal accuracy either, you just aim in a Nazi’s general direction and drop them (good thing too since there’s no iron sight or crosshairs). STORY:  Kill Nazis go!  You’re a captured spy and the game contains 6 episodes of 10 floors each.  Episode 1 has you tasked with escaping while the others have other objectives such as killing various madmen bosses, including Hitler. GRAPHICS:  They’re bad.  There’s not even a texture for the entire floor or ceiling.  It’s the flattest looking 3-D game you’ll ever see.  But 3 dimensions had to start somewhere and you’re looking at it here.  There’s no resolution or graphics options at all. PERFORMANCE:  This didn’t even tax computers 20 years ago.  It launches in DOSbox and ran perfectly for me. SOUND:  Better than the graphics and there are some memorable Nazi death cries.  The music is creepy yet fun at the same type, a military style and it works well. REPLAYABILITY:  Other than the curiosity or nostalgia factor there is a scoring system and secrets to find but it’s unlikely many people would be compelled to keep playing.  But any FPS fan or retro gamer should at least try this. SIMILAR TO:  Doom, Star Wars Dark Forces, Shadow Warrior RECOMMENDED PURCHASE PRICE:  <$5 (often included in Doom promotions) TITLE:  Wolfenstein 3D DEVELOPER:  id Software RELEASED:  1992 (Steam page is incorrect) 80/100

title: Wolfenstein 3D
text: Wolfenstein 3D was the game that jump started the first person shooter genre. Often mistaken as the first game to utilize the concept of a shooter game in first person perspective for gameplay as oppose to third person perspective. However the first first person shooter games were the 1974 "Maze War" & "Spasim". Anyways Wolfenstein 3D is the third game in the Wolfenstein franchise, the first two were the 1981 "Castle Wolfenstein" & the 1984 "Beyond Castle Wolfenstein". For this game it dropped the word "castle" and added "3-D" at the end. Making games in a 3-D perspective was still a primative attempt for game developers back then, something that is common to see in games today, but back then gamers were amazed to play through levels that felt like going through actual rooms. The plot is very basic, you assumed the role of an American Polish WW2 soldier named  William "B.J." Blazkowicz who must escape a castle conterted into a prison called Castle Wolfenstein that's heavily occupied by SS officiers. B.J. must kill various enemies in order to escape the castle alive. The release of this game has inspired various future first person shooter games and even provided inspiration for various war genre games. Wolfenstein is an important piece of gaming history that all gamers should experience. It's a fun and rewarding experience with various weapons and treasure to collect in various floors of Nazi occupied headquarters.

title: Wolfenstein: The New Order
text: (no spoilers) What a disappointment, this game is a complete miss and I have no idea how it has so positive rating. I played the original game, and I played and loved Return to Casle Wolfenstein back when it came out. But this game is a mockery to both its prequels. Wolfenstein: The New Order is a story driven adventure/fps. It plays like a mix of Bioshock Infinite, Duke Nukem Forever and Call of Duty 1, with absolutely everything that this would imply: -The gameplay is extremely fragmented, heavily depending on scripts, full of some stupid minigames and passages where you do absolutely nothing but walk on highlighted path, push an action key or just give a hand to someone. Levels are often visually grand but you cannot go anywhere except the one small path you have to take. -This is 100% story driven game, full of long cutscenes. The problem is, the story is absolutely terrible nonsense, seriously. I was glad at first they decided to go with "alternative history", since that is way better imo than to molest actual history. But the storyline is completely idiotic on all levels: It fails as a sci-fi as it makes no sense whatsoever and ignores completely both history and the laws of physics (without any exaggeration, even Bioshock Infinite has a much more inteligent and believeable story...Yea, crazy, I know!), it fails also as a story as the characters are flat, stupid, and all talk like in a Disney fairy tale. There are even (wishfully) romantic scenes in the story...HAHAHA!  I wont go into any details on the story to avoid spoilers, but I guarantee you, you will be laughing your back off at moments which the developers tried hard to be brutal or hearthbreaking. Again,  - there are many stealth parts in this game, but they are a complete joke (just imagine Mafia 3 stealth play) - you lose all your stuff between almost every mission, and have to start with a knife almost every mission. Not terrible on it's own, but it makes searching for ammo and weapons a waste of time in this game. I honestly cannot think of one strong upside of this game, only things that are not horrible. The weapons feel phony and I found most of them boring. Most of the enemies look, move and die the same so the gun side of this game feels very repetetive. I like the checkpoints system (no quick save). The visuals are pretty good, some of the levels are nicely detailed. I liked the perks and also hunting for hidden collectibles. The nostalgic levels from first Wolfenstein were a nice touch too. I recommend not buying this game, certainly not for more than 10 usd, it is not worth more. If you are looking for a decent adventure/fps story driven game with romantic elements, get Bioshock Infinite. Also, I just read that they are planning a sequel to this game, pretty much in the same spirit as this pathetic mess. So rip Wolfenstein series, we will never forget (*your first 2 games!)... (apologies for bad grammar)

title: Wolfenstein: The New Order
text: Wolfenstein: The New Order is a easily one of the best FPSes of the year. The shooting itself is so satisfying that it easily stays fresh for at least two playthroughs. Add some nice level design, multitude of weapons, a lot of gore and a lengthy campaign, and you have an awesome game that is very easy to recommend for fans of the genre. A good comparison to make here is with the new Shadow Warrior: it takes the gameplay to new directions while it does not forget it roots. For this reason, I wouldn't call the New Order an old-school FPS but thankfully, it is FAR away from the typical, dumbed-down modern shooter. I have only three gripes with the game: - I hope it won't come in a DLC or something but when you establish a really twisted boss throughout the game (and I'm not talking about Totenkopf), it is downright painful to see that character (though not unscratched) get away . - While the levels are varied enough, there were some opportunities that the developers missed out on especially if we look at how over-the-top the game is. For example, if you put us on the Moon, have some nice fights on the surface with low gravity or something! (Instead of just shooting down three drones over the course of 2 minutes...) - The game presents two timelines that are essentially two playthroughs, however the differences are just too small to bother. Sure, it is worth is because of the gunplay, but it would have been nice if at least some of the scenes are different. (Apart from meeting another side-character and getting another type of collectible, it is pretty much the same. Wyatt and Fergus even say some of the same lines, like how both are mad at you for making the wrong choice.) But these are just very small concerns for an otherwise fantastic game. While I am a bit hesitant recommending it at €50, I got it during the Steam Sale for half its price, and I must say it was very, very worth it. P.S.: I can't stress enough how satisfying the shooting is. Seriously, dual-wielding shotguns (one that shoots the regular pellets, the other shooting ricocheting pellets) and mowing down a bunch of enemies is majestic.

title: Wolfenstein: The New Order

title: Wolfenstein: The New Order
text: A solid addition to the FPS genre. You are William J Blazkowicz, a Nazi killing machine. In this alternative time line, in which the 3rd Reich wins World War II, Blazkowicz lays dormant in a mental hospital. 14 years pass, and he is awakened and once again called about to battle the forces of evil. Wolfenstein: The New Order is a worthy continuation of the Wolfenstein series. A classic first person shooter with all the usual tropes: big guns, tons of ammo, nigh-impervious hero, and thumping music. Tear through rooms of enemies soliders filling em with hot lead, or, when given the opportunity, skulk around unseen and have your knife silence your foes. The game is gritty while embracing the absurd (though, I won't spoil more than that). But there is more to wolfenstein than a pile of bodies. The story is deeper than the old school FPS and present the player with 2 times lines which provide different characters, some bonuses (one contains armor upgrades, the other health) and occasionally different ways to play through levels. Though I felt they could have done a lot more with this concept in regards to game play, it was a surprising element that simply left me wanting more. The game does a decent job of variety while not over staying it's welcome. Weapons have alternative fire, alternative versions and dual wielding, so the player has a variety of load outs at their disposal. Aside from larger than necessary gun models and explaining how to dual-alt fire (perhaps I missed the message in game) I don't have any complaints. There are automatic save checkpoints which are fairly distributed, however there are times they occur in poor conjunction with cut-scenes. Sometimes you are forced to play a cut-scene over and over (the skip function is hit or miss as the game is loading during some of these scenes) which can be annoying. Other times, the save occur after a scripted interaction, and upon reloading, that interaction disappears (costing you items) or the save happens after a battle but before you stock up on items. So upon death, you get to stock up again and again... and again. Enemies are relatively fair - they have terrible peripheral vision to enable a lot of leeway in stealth, though the ability to see through smoke which can leave the player at a massive disadvantage. The stealth portions aren't mandatory but it's noticeable when the game expects you to play to that style. The perks system provide the player with additional bonuses upon being unlocked, but play style is dictated by the situation more so than player preference. Uber can be a challenge (particularly if you haven't unlocked all the perks) but if that's still not enough, the enigma codes provide players with alternative modes of play, if you find all the codes and figure out how to unlock them. Wolfenstein is an excellent game with a few surprises to go along with its solid genre defining elements. I hope future iterations expand about the alternative time line and maybe clean up some of the problems I had with auto-saving but it was predominantly positive and fun gaming experience.

text: TANKS TANKS TANKS> This is basically World of Tanks lite. A mobile game port for the computer. It's a great 7v7, quick, fast games of explosions and manuvere tactics. So choose between German, France, USSR, China, UK and USA tanks and battle. The tanks for all countries break down to light, medium and heavy tanks. Each tank has ( and countries) type of tank are designed with specific  playing style. But it really comes down to how good are you? your skills? Understanding your tanks ability and type of ammo/shooting and tactic, manuvereing is all key. LOCATION X 3. Yes, that saying, is how you play this game. There are daily missions and a tuturial mission to start you off with good gold/silver for upgrades or research points. Research unlocks tanks or crew skills, and gold/silver gets your tanks provisions, ammo,equipment, and camo. Its all about making your tank the best in every way possible to get that edge in battle. Faster reload or faster repairing? ammo penetration rounds or explosive rounds? Make your tank the way you want with upgrades. Very custimizable. Plenty of camo skins so you look ''individual'' as you can as a heap of moving gun and metal...The maps are neat and with plenty of hiding, ambushing or sniper points for you tank. Games are a capture the point or destroy all other team tanks...up to you. Have fun and hear that BOOM! of your tanks gun, with the gunman yelling PENETRATION!

title: World of Tanks Blitz
text: This is just a shooter but instead of a guy you have a tank. It's also arena combat, so forget strategy, there is none. The game is designed to encourage..err... almost force you to spend your hard earn real life cash. This is an archaic form of game that dies out very fast as people get sick of the greedy nature of the game designers and publisher. Look at League of Legend and Guild Wars, they do not have a crappy system that "forces" you to spend money, they give you the opportunity to buy stuff you like. For example, you have experience and "free" experience instead of having just one experience pool but you gain less, and to convert experience into "free" experience, you need to spend real life money for something that should already be part of the game (like you can convert 5 to 1 normal experience to free experience). I really hope nobody uses these scamming "services"... unless they like getting screwed. Some tanks are ranked higher than they should and ends up being totally useless on the battle field, especially unresearched (Like Pz2, all American Tanks level 2 to 4, etc.). They have some serious balancing isssues to fix. The game designers are ignorant of WWII tanks. For example, there were no Pzkw-IVa or b in action at all in WWII, yet the designers put that one in the game which makes no sense since they are bad tanks. Games are short 5-10 min. Good part is that if your tank is destroyed, you can go back to your garage and pick another fight. There are some major flaws in the game : - Slope armour is not taken into account . Which is dumb because it was a major factor in the German-Russian war with the T-34. Hetzer, Panther, Jagd Pather and other tanks using slope armour are highly underevaluated. They do not seem to understand that sloped armour like doubles its efficiency. - They mix tanks categories which leads to no damage done for the lighter tanks to the heavier tanks. This is especially true for light tanks. The light tanks should only fight light tanks. - They mix eras. A 1939 tank would have no chance against a 1944-45 tank. Hetzer would be practically invulnerable to 1939 tanks, yet it is mixed with such tanks. And this happens in the game. I use a Pz II Luchs and it cannot harm anyone so I do not get any experience to get a better gun due to this stupidity. There should be two types of arenas, mixed and scaled+historical. That way, light tanks would not fight medium and heavy tanks. No way a Pz 2 or a T-24 can harm a heavy and even less a super heavy tank. Hetzers are so underevaluated. It was capable of rolling at 42 km/h which is nice considering the tanks that it was pitted against. - Shooting in the butt of a tank should do serious damage when there is penetration, but in this game, you just lose hps. Lame. If you are very lucky, you do some special effect like ingniting the fuel reserves or something. It happens not enough time to be important not to expose the back of your tank and people just move however they please. Sure, you lose more hps but it is not that serious. - Makes me laugh when I see a Stug having more protection than late war machines like the Hetzer or as much as the Jagd Panther. haha! Makes completely no sense. - Some tanks are supposed to be fast like the Hetzer... yes him again. lol - Oh! And StuG are better than late war weapons like the Hetzer and T-34. lol - Pzkw-IVa and b were more a training units and prototypes and practically saw no action. The Pzkw-IVc was the main support tank of the German Reich in 1939. The Pzfw-IVc to Pzkw-IVf used short barrels making them useless at long range and very imprecise, which is not the case in this game since you can snipe someone far away with an untrained crew on top of that and hit 80% of the time... hahaha! Stupid game and lame game designers that did not do their research properly. There were only 35 Pzkw-IVa produced in the entire world in history. There were practically no Pzkw-IVb produced. Pzkw-IVc was the one mass produced. Only the Pzkw-IVf2 was equiped with a long barrel gun which then changed the way the Pzkw-IV was used resulting in very interesting designs afterwards. But in this game that designers know nothing about WWII, the Pzkw-IVa is a main battle tank. hahaha! And the tank sucks royally and should be replaced like in real life with the Pzkw-IVc! - Point Blank shot in the butt of a super light tank with a 75mm AP shell and it does nothing? Perhaps in the front with slope armour, but in the back? A flat back on top of that? Go back to school designers, your game is super dumb and proves your ignorance. I know they are trying to make tank platoons, but at the very least, categorize the tanks per year dont put early war tanks with late war tanks, none of those were used and they would have had no chance with 1944-45 technology. All in all I don't recommand this game since it's just another arena shooter that brings nothing new to the genre. There are thousands of those that have appeared since the 1990s. It is also a pay to win but you can play for a long time for free like League of Legends for example. If you are in no hurry, you can progres slowly and avoid premium accounts who doubles your xps. Prices are hilarious. They ask more money than big games like World of Warcraft or other MMOs. With the price they are asking, you can buy six good games on Steam for the same price. lol Also, unlike League of Legends, I doubt I will play years of this game. Do not play this if you play Unreal or some other great shooter already, really not worth your time.

title: World of Warships
text: Uninstalled the original client so that I could install this via steam, only to find out that I can't even use my original account and have to be forced to make a new account. Teaches me to probably read a few more reviews before just going nuts and uninstalling the original client. After many years of playing on 1 account, unlocking various ships of various nations. I don't need another only to start over from scratch. Uninstalled.... Back to original client... Edit: Since people would rather have my opinion of the game. I will say this. The game is definitely worth playing. Don't get me wrong. Great graphics, great strategic gameplay, and plenty of ships to grind on various beautiful looking maps. I've played this game on and off for years, (Since Closed Alpha), and I will continue to play it. World of warships as a whole gets my Recommended rating. The fact that veteran players who have been asking for steam integration for years, are forced to create a new account is absolute crap. Sure, you can do some majic, delete some files, and poof you can log into your account. Having to go about it that way, shows me the devs are lazy if you can go around easily bypassing their forced steam login. But that's no surprise there I guess, though Wargaming overall I've always supported in one way or another. But the decision to make the Steam Client and the WoWs client was a poor decision in my opinion. Just splits and spreads the playerbase out on more servers that can't even cross play with one another. I do hope to see some improvements in the future. But coming from a vet player, this was a major dissapointment when finding out this information.

Sure its basicallly war thunder on the sea but, when you play its really fun. People Are not happy about losing their accounts. Luckily i just found this game a few days ago on steam. So  For My Experience ingame I Recommend This game. 8/10 Reasons : +Graphics +Good Community (Actually work together) +Auto Pilot +Amazing 3 D Mini Map -No link account -*When Starting*Small amount of XP (Encouraging Pay to Progress)

title: World of Warships
text: Sure, they've made it clear that you can't use your previous wargaming account on the steam version, but that doesn't mean that said fact isn't a poor decision in my opinion. For a new player this doesn't matter much, but for players that previously have played World of Warships this means the Steam version of the game offers NOTHING except a clean start. If that's what you're looking for as an old player then sure, it's a thumbs up. For other older players of WoWs like me a game that offers nothing can't get any recommendation at all, leaving "no" as the only recommendation option for the steam version of this game.

text: Have mixed feelings so far about this game. My system has the power to play the game under ultra settings but yet I play under 1080I. I can run three games and then the game just crashes out from under me. When in game and playing the game play is enjoyable and the graphics and options are so great that this game has great potential that I will work and figure out if the bugs are on my end or have to summit a ticket. I would say give this game a chance.
